issue.title: Spike an explicit instruction channel for agy (Antigravity) so it can receive the SASE bundle instead of native AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md discovery
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1lj.2 (note #2) while working epic sase-1lj (E4); triaged and filed by
the sase-1lj land agent. The E4 plan's design decision D4 asked phase workers to record
this spike as a follow-up.

E4 keeps agy (Antigravity CLI 1.4.0), Qwen, and OpenCode on native `AGENTS.md` discovery
(`provider_legacy`) because agy reads both `GEMINI.md` and `AGENTS.md`, walking from the
cwd up to the repo root, and offers no flag to suppress those rules and no
system-prompt flag. Delivering a per-invocation prefix bundle would therefore load the
contract twice. E4's `E4 PROBES:` (sase-1lj.2 note #1) confirmed that agy answers from
`AGENTS.md` alone and loads both files when both exist. agy is about 106 runs in 30 days.

Spike: find whether agy has a usable explicit instruction channel, for example custom
agents' `CustomAgentSystemPromptConfig`, `.agents/rules/` scoping, or a settings key
that disables workspace rule discovery. Check whether that channel can (a) carry the
SASE bundle with the home layer, which agy lacks today, and (b) make the home
`GEMINI.md` copy redundant ahead of E5. Record the outcome against the reopen trigger
in `decisions:readable-agents-md` ("a legacy CLI gains a suppression switch or a
system-prompt channel").

task_type_fields.proposal: Probe agy 1.4.0+ for an explicit instruction/system-prompt channel (for example CustomAgentSystemPromptConfig) or a rule-discovery suppression switch, and if one works, wire agy to receive the per-invocation SASE bundle (with the home layer) without double-loading the contract.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: E4 (sase-1lj) explicitly kept agy, Qwen, and OpenCode on native AGENTS.md discovery (D4) and put explicit delivery for those CLIs out of scope; this is a reopen-trigger investigation for decisions:readable-agents-md.

issue.creation_reason: E4 design decision D4 left agy on native discovery for lack of a suppression switch; its phase worker proposed probing for an explicit channel, which is outside E4's scope.
